extra.message: The JWT signing secret ('token.secret: abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz') is a hardcoded, weak, publicly-known default value shipped in the repo. It is loaded via @Value("${token.secret}") in ruoyi-framework/src/main/java/com/ruoyi/framework/web/service/TokenService.java (fields at lines 42-43) and used to sign (lines 179-185, HS512) and verify (lines 193-199) every session token. Any deployment that does not override this value allows an attacker to forge arbitrary JWTs (including for the admin account) and fully bypass authentication.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: generatorCode(tableName) writes a rendered Velocity template to a filesystem path built by getGenPath() (lines 555-563: genPath + File.separator + VelocityUtils.getFileName(...)) and VelocityUtils.getFileName() (ruoyi-generator/.../util/VelocityUtils.java lines 199-277), which concatenates the table's packageName/moduleName/businessName/className fields with zero validation against '../' or absolute-path sequences. These fields (and genPath itself) are fully attacker-controlled via PUT /tool/gen (GenController.editSave -> validateEdit, which only checks tree/sub-table fields, never packageName/moduleName/businessName/genPath). When gen.allowOverwrite is enabled (generator.yml), GET /tool/gen/genCode/{tableName} (requires only 'tool:gen:code' permission, not admin) lets an authenticated low-privilege user write arbitrary content to an arbitrary file path on the server, e.g. by setting genPath="/some/absolute/path" or packageName="../../../../etc".

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: writeToZip() creates ZIP entries using `new ZipEntry(fileName)` where fileName comes directly from VelocityUtils.getFileName(template, table) (ruoyi-generator/.../util/VelocityUtils.java lines 199-277), built from the unsanitized, user-settable packageName/moduleName/businessName fields of GenTable. This is reachable unauthenticated of any 'allowOverwrite' gate via GET /tool/gen/download/{tableName} and /tool/gen/batchGenCode (only 'tool:gen:code' permission required). An attacker who controls those fields can craft ZIP entry names containing '../' sequences (zip-slip), so that extracting the generated archive with a naive unzip tool overwrites files outside the intended output directory on whichever machine extracts it.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The noticeContent field (rich-text announcement body, set/read via setNoticeContent/getNoticeContent) has no @Xss validation or any sanitization, unlike noticeTitle which is protected by @Xss (line 54, 'noticeTitle' getter). In addition, the application's global XSS filter deliberately excludes this exact endpoint: ruoyi-admin/src/main/resources/application.yml line 145 sets `xss.excludes: /system/notice`, so POST/PUT /system/notice (SysNoticeController.add/edit) bypass XssHttpServletRequestWrapper entirely for this path. Any authenticated user holding the 'system:notice:add' or 'system:notice:edit' permission can therefore store arbitrary HTML/JavaScript in noticeContent, which is later displayed to every user who views the notice list/detail (e.g. GET /system/notice/listTop), resulting in persistent stored XSS against all users including admins.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The Druid StatViewServlet monitoring console (enabled, url-pattern /druid/*) has an empty IP allow-list (line 47, which per the adjacent comment means 'allow access from any IP') and hardcoded, weak default login credentials login-username: ruoyi / login-password: 123456 (lines 50-51). Spring Security also explicitly permits all unauthenticated access to /druid/** (ruoyi-framework/src/main/java/com/ruoyi/framework/config/SecurityConfig.java line 106). Any remote attacker who guesses or finds these well-known default credentials gets full access to the SQL monitoring console, exposing executed SQL statements, bind parameters, data source URLs, and connection pool internals.

The primary MySQL datasource credentials (username: root, password: password) are hardcoded in plaintext in the shipped configuration file, disclosing a production-capable root database credential to anyone with source access.

The global CorsFilter bean allows any origin (addAllowedOriginPattern("*")), any header, and any method, mapped to all paths (source.registerCorsConfiguration("/**", config)). This removes same-origin protection for every endpoint in the application, letting any third-party website issue cross-origin requests against the API.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
